Laura —

We're seeing a sustained p95 jump and a burst of 502s coming from our private deployment (cluster: lynxbridge-prod-vpc, region us-west-2). The window started ~08:15 and by 08:30 we've had recurring 502s and user-facing latency skyrocketed (p50 ~180ms -> 600ms, p95 ~1.8s -> 6.2s). Throughput dropped by ~25% as requests are timing out and the queue grows.

Attached is a Grafana snapshot showing the p95 and 502 surge (grafana_p95_20261110.png). We're about to put this in front of our ops team but need Redwood's immediate triage — this is impacting our main checkout flow. No recent customer traffic pattern changes on our side. We did receive a Redwood runtime package update last night but haven't rolled anything since.

Can you confirm whether this looks like a kernel/runtime regression on your side? If you have a recommended mitigation (fallback model variant, routing to dedicated pool), we need it ASAP.

Thanks,
Sasha Turner

Looping in some early telemetry from our end after correlating the customer's grafana with our private control plane logs:
- Audit snippet shows a steady KV-cache growth on the shard group serving LynxBridge around 07:50–09:10, concurrent with an increase in long tail decode durations. I've attached a short CSV extract (audit_log_snippet.csv).
- There are traces of decoder worker queueing and rare 502s that align with kernel path switchovers on a subset of GPU nodes (suspect quantized kernel path).

Initial recommendation (short window mitigation):
- Apply a rolling revert of last night's runtime patch to nodes in group A (small batch) to confirm whether p95 drops.
- Activate traffic shaping: shift 25–40% of traffic to a fallback model variant (lower-precision) while nodes are remediated.
- Force a KV cache eviction for the hottest prefixes (minimizes coldstart impact if we fall back).

If this is a kernel/quant path mismatch, the rollback should materially reduce 5xx/latency. I'll start preparing the audit snippet and open a hotfix runbook.

Subject: Re: Production degradation — private cluster (p95 up, 502s)

Quick technical readout from infra:
- Root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel path is hitting a lock/contention pattern on a specific GPU driver version we rolled out last night. That causes decoder worker stalls under tail-heavy request patterns, which then backpressure the front-end and surface as 502s when timeouts accrue.
- Confirmed: the affected nodes show elevated kernel switch counts and slower memcpy times.

Remediation plan (recommended, ETA 2–3 hours):
1) Roll back runtime kernel to previous verified revision on a small canary subset (group A). Observe p95 for 20 mins.
2) If canary shows p95 improvement, proceed with rolling revert across pool (staggered 10% batches).
3) While rolling revert is in progress, shift 30% traffic to the lower-precision fallback variant (no model retrain needed) to relieve queue pressure.
4) Prepare a rolling restart of the hot nodes after revert to drain in-flight KV state; schedule during low-risk windows per customer preference.

Resource asks: two SREs on hotfix (apply revert + roll), one infra engineer to monitor kernel metrics, and CS to coordinate customer communications. I’ve created the incident ticket RED-8821 and linked the audit snippet.

If we get exec approval to prioritize, we can start step 1 immediately.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Summary: LynxBridge (DB-9421) reported a sustained p95 and an uptick in 502s this morning on their private VPC cluster (us-west-2). Early telemetry points to a kernel/runtime path mismatch on a subset of GPU nodes that correlates with last night's runtime rollout. Customer impact: main checkout flow affected, throughput down ~25%, visible p95 spike to ~6s and repeated 502s between 08:15–09:10 PST.

Proposed immediate actions (need exec prioritization):
- Apply an emergency rollback of the runtime kernel on a canary subset and, if successful, roll across the pool (Jonas estimates 2–3 hours total).
- Shift 30% of customer traffic to a lower-precision fallback variant while we remediate.
- Allocate 2 SREs + 1 infra engineer to the hotfix; CS (Marissa) will coordinate messaging and potential SLA credit if remediation extends.

Customer is asking for a timeline and mitigation now; they have agreed to fallback routing if we can provide an ETA. Failure to remediate promptly will likely trigger an SLA credit conversation.

Request: approve hotfix priority and resource assignment so we can start the canary rollback. I’ve attached the Grafana snapshot and audit snippet in the incident ticket and linked RED-8821.
